Fit continuous-time movement models to each track with ctmm

Source: R/ctmm_tt_fit.R
ctmm_tt_fit.Rd

This function fits a continuous-time movement model, using the package ctmm, to each track of a tibble of tracks. The fitted models are returned in a tibble with one row per track, in the same order as the tracks in the metadata (see show_meta()), so that they can be easily combined with the metadata for further analyses. The table of models is the starting point for the analyses that rely on ctmm, such as the estimation of home ranges with autocorrelated kernel density estimation (hr_tt_akde()).

Usage

ctmm_tt_fit(
  x,
  model = "auto",
  error = FALSE,
  uere = NULL,
  ic = "AICc",
  candidates = FALSE,
  error_cols = "auto",
  cores = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object, in a projected coordinate reference system with units in metres. It can be grouped by its track id column, but not by other variables (see Details).

model

The movement model to fit. Either one of:

  • "auto" (the default): select the best model with ctmm::ctmm.select(), which starts from the model suggested by the variogram of the track (generally an anisotropic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck foraging process), and fits simpler models (e.g. isotropic, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, or independent locations) until the information criterion no longer improves.

  • "iid": independent and identically distributed locations (i.e. no autocorrelation).

  • "ou": Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (autocorrelated positions, with a home range).

  • "ouf": Ornstein-Uhlenbeck foraging process (autocorrelated positions and velocities, with a home range).

  • "bm": Brownian motion (no home range).

  • a model template created with ctmm::ctmm(), which is fitted to every track with ctmm::ctmm.fit().

  • a list of such templates, one per track, either named by track id or in the order of the metadata.

error

Logical; whether to fit a model of location error. If the tracks have information on the error of each location (e.g. dilution of precision, see error_cols), it is used by the error model. With a model template, error = TRUE adds the error model to the template, unless the template already has one (e.g. ctmm::ctmm(error = TRUE)); with error = FALSE, the error model of the template (if any) is kept.

uere

A User Equivalent Range Error (in metres) used to calibrate the location error (see ctmm::uere()), or an object created with ctmm::uere.fit() from calibration data. If set, the error model is fitted (i.e. error is set to TRUE), also for model templates.

ic

The information criterion used to select the best model when model = "auto" (see ctmm::ctmm.select()). Default is "AICc".

candidates

Logical; if TRUE and model = "auto", all the candidate models fitted by ctmm::ctmm.select(), ranked by ic, are returned in the list-column candidates. Default is FALSE.

error_cols

The columns of the event data with information on the error of the locations, passed to mt_as_telemetry(). The same columns are used by the other functions that use the fitted models.

cores

The number of cores used by ctmm::ctmm.select() to fit the candidate models in parallel (only used with model = "auto").

...

Additional arguments passed to ctmm::ctmm.select() (if model = "auto") or ctmm::ctmm.fit() (otherwise), e.g. method or control.

Value

A tibble of class ctmm_tt_fit_tbl, with one row per track, in the order of the metadata, and columns:

  • the track id column (as named in x)

  • model: a list-column of the fitted ctmm models (NULL if the model could not be fitted)

  • model_name: the name of the fitted model (e.g. "OUF anisotropic")

  • aicc: the corrected Akaike Information Criterion of the fitted model

  • dof_area: the effective number of degrees of freedom for the estimate of the home range area (small values, e.g. below 5-10, imply very uncertain home range estimates)

  • n_events, t_start, t_end: the number of events with a location used to fit the model, and the time of the first and last event; these are used by other functions to check that the tracks have not changed since the models were fitted

  • fit_message: NA, or the error message if the model could not be fitted

  • candidates (only if candidates = TRUE): a list-column of the candidate models

The coordinate reference system of x and the error columns used are stored as attributes of the table.

Details

Fitting is done in two steps, as recommended by ctmm: first, initial values of the parameters are guessed from the empirical variogram of each track (ctmm::ctmm.guess()), and then the model is fitted by maximum likelihood (ctmm::ctmm.fit()). With model = "auto" (the default), a series of candidate models is fitted and the best one is selected based on an information criterion (ctmm::ctmm.select()). This is the most appropriate approach in most cases, but it can be slow for long tracks. It is always good practice to inspect the fit of the models (e.g. by comparing the variogram of each track with the fitted model, see the "Movement models with ctmm" article).

Models are fitted to each track separately. To fit models at a different level (e.g. to each trip, or to each season of a track), first make that level the track of x, e.g. with tt_split_trips() or move2::mt_set_track_id().

The track data are converted with mt_as_telemetry(), so x must be in a projected coordinate reference system with units in metres (see mt_as_telemetry() for details).

If the model cannot be fitted for a track (e.g. because the track has too few locations), a warning is given, and the track is kept in the table with a NULL model, and the error message in column fit_message, so that the table always has one row per track in the metadata. Warnings raised by ctmm while fitting are reported with the id of the track.

See also

ctmm_tt_summary() to summarise the parameters of the models, hr_tt_akde() to estimate home ranges from the models.

Examples

# the buffalo dataset from ctmm, converted to a tibble of tracks
data(buffalo, package = "ctmm")
buffalo_tt <- mt_as_move2(buffalo)
# we use a subset of the first two buffalo to make the example fast
buffalo_sub <- buffalo_tt %>%
  filter_by_meta(track %in% c("Cilla", "Gabs")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(track) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 100) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
buffalo_fit <- ctmm_tt_fit(buffalo_sub, model = "ou")
#> Minimum sampling interval of 59 minutes in Cilla
#> Minimum sampling interval of 57 minutes in Gabs
buffalo_fit
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   track model      model_name  aicc dof_area n_events t_start                   
#>   <fct> <named li> <chr>      <dbl>    <dbl>    <int> <dttm>                    
#> 1 Cilla <ctmm>     OU anisot… 3114.     3.29      100 2005-07-14 05:35:00.000000
#> 2 Gabs  <ctmm>     OU anisot… 2875.     1.68      100 2005-04-05 05:56:00.000000
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: t_end <dttm>, fit_message <chr>
